title: Starter telemetry & first-touch blueprint (quickjump)
content:
Purpose:
Lightweight, copyable blueprint to get a new SDK integration instrumented, visible, and safe in the first 15 minutes. Target audience: SDK authors, integrator engineers, and solutions engineers doing a live embed or first-customer demo.

Context / problem we solve:
- New SDKs and starter apps often ship without useful telemetry; first-touch debugging is slow and product telemetry gaps delay rollouts.
- Teams need a minimal set of events, a tiny sample app, and a short runbook so on-call/support can triage immediately.

Goals (v0):
1) Provide a 3-minute smoke telemetry checklist that can be copy-pasted into any starter repo.
2) Ship a 15-minute path: sample app + dashboards + simple alert.
3) Reduce mean time to identify SDK failures on first deploy from hours -> <15 minutes.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Minimal event set and naming conventions
- Example SDK snippets (JS + Python) for emitting events to our observability pipeline
- Dashboard tiles and a simple alerts matrix
- Runbook checklist for first-touch incidents and demo prep
- TODO: later — richer privacy/KMS guidance, sampling strategies, offline buffering options

Quick summary checklist (copy-paste):
- [ ] Add SDK telemetry helper (function trackEvent(name, props))
- [ ] Emit these events: sdk.init, sdk.request.start, sdk.request.end, sdk.error, sdk.cache.hit
- [ ] Add correlation_id to every event (trace_id or request_id)
- [ ] Create dashboard: last 30m success rate, p50/p90 latency, error stream
- [ ] Create alert: error rate > 3% for 5m or p95 latency > 2s for 10m

Minimal event schema (single-line examples):
- sdk.init -> {"event":"sdk.init","sdk_name":"redwood-js","version":"0.1.3","environment":"sandbox","ts":...}
- sdk.request.start -> {"event":"sdk.request.start","request_id":"r_123","model":"redwood-1","route":"/chat","user_id":"u_987","ts":...}
- sdk.request.end -> {"event":"sdk.request.end","request_id":"r_123","status":"ok|error","tokens":45,"latency_ms":412,"ts":...}
- sdk.error -> {"event":"sdk.error","request_id":"r_123","err_code":"timeout|quota|validation","message":"...","stack":"...","ts":...}
- sdk.cache.hit -> {"event":"sdk.cache.hit","request_id":"r_321","cache_layer":"prefix","ts":...}

Event naming notes (short):
- Use lower-dash names, start with sdk.* to keep queries scoped.
- Keep properties flat (no nested objects) to make dashboards friendly.
- Correlate using request_id + user_id. Always include sdk.version when possible.

Instrumentation snippets (JS):
- minimal helper (pseudo):
  function trackEvent(name, props) {
    // lightweight, async fire-and-forget
    fetch(process.env.TELEMETRY_URL, {method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({event:name, ...props})}).catch(()=>{});
  }

- usage pattern:
  trackEvent('sdk.init', {sdk_name:'redwood-js', version: pkg.version, environment:process.env.ENV});
  const reqId = genId();
  trackEvent('sdk.request.start', {request_id:reqId, model, route, user_id});
  // after call
  trackEvent('sdk.request.end', {request_id:reqId, status:'ok', latency_ms:latMs, tokens});

Instrumentation snippet (Python):
  import requests
  def track_event(name, props):
      try:
          requests.post(os.environ['TELEMETRY_URL'], json=dict(event=name, **props), timeout=0.5)
      except Exception:
          pass

Telemetry transport rules (practical):
- Fire-and-forget over HTTPS, non-blocking. If network fails, swallow (do not break app).
- Respect environment variable TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true for privacy-controlled demos.
- Sample at 1% by default for production-high-volume flows; for quickstart keep full sampling to make dashboards useful.

Dashboard (30-minute sprint):
Tiles to create in order:
1) Real-time error stream (filter event=sdk.error) + fast link to raw logs
2) Success rate: count(sdk.request.end where status=ok) / total rps, last 30m
3) Latency histogram/p95 for sdk.request.end latency_ms
4) Top error codes (group by err_code)
5) Recent init versions (group by sdk.version)

Alerting quick defaults:
- P1-ish demo alert: error rate >= 3% sustained for 5m -> page on-call developer
- P2: p95 latency > 2s for 10m -> slack #devexp-alerts + email to feature owner
- P3: spike in sdk.init with older version -> notification to integrations lead

First-touch runbook (for on-call / SE during demo):
1) Confirm environment and API keys (env variables set correctly)
2) Check dashboard: error stream -> click into earliest error -> correlate request_id
3) If timeout errors: check routing and region fallback logs (JIRA tag: INFRA-REGION)
4) If validation errors: check client SDK payload, compare against sample template in README
5) If high latency: try reproduce via curl with same payload and headers; toggle caching off/on to compare
6) Rollback path: switch to a pinned model variant or fallback route that uses a known-good endpoint

Demo prep checklist (5 minutes):
- Clear stale keys, set TELEMETRY_DISABLED=false for demo (or use demo-only telemetry URL)
- Warm KV cache with 3 canned calls (see /tools/warmup)
- Confirm dashboard time window and pinned filters (route=demo-sample)
- Have fallback script ready: curl fallback endpoint and a local stub server snippet

Sample README snippet to include in starter repo:
"""
Quick telemetry (copy into .env):
TELEMETRY_URL=https://telemetry.redwood.internal/ingest
TELEMETRY_DISABLED=false

1) Install helper and call trackEvent at SDK bootstrap and request boundaries.
2) Use request_id for correlation.
3) If you need to opt-out for privacy demos set TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true.
"""

Safety, privacy, and PII notes (short):
- Never send raw user content. Redact prompt/text fields before sending. Send hashes for correlation if needed.
- If a customer requires no telemetry, set TELEMETRY_DISABLED and offer an offline retention mode (local file buffer) — TODO in roadmap.

Rollout & ownership (v0):
- Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-developer-experience)
- Integrations lead (onboarding): Miguel Ruiz
- SRE / observability contact: Dana Cho
- Recommended rollout steps: add helper -> add events to starter -> create dashboard templates -> enable in CI smoke tests

Examples of concrete tickets to create (templates):
- DEVEXP-telemetry-setup-<repo>: Add minimal telemetry helper and README snippet (owner: repo maintainer)
- DEVEXP-dashboard-<repo>: Create dashboard with tiles 1-5 and alert rules (owner: observability)
- DEVEXP-demo-telemetry-check: Pre-demo checklist run and warmup script (owner: SE running demo)

Open questions / followups (short):
- Sampling defaults per SDK language (how aggressive for mobile vs server?)
- Best safe-hash algo for user identifiers we can standardize on (sha256 vs blake2?)
- Should we provide a tiny npm/pip package that wraps the helper and offers toggles? (pro: copy-paste, con: maintenance)

Next actions (first sprint):
- [Aisha] Create starter telemetry npm package (v0) with trackEvent helper — ETA 2w
- [Miguel] Add telemetry hooks to three starter repos (js, python, dotnet) — ETA 1w
- [Dana] Create dashboard templates and alert recipes in observability — ETA 3 days
- [Zoe] Draft privacy-safe guidance and README blurb — ETA 1w

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep examples tiny — developers copy instead of ignoring.
- Aim for default-on telemetry in sandbox, default-off in prod for privacy-sensitive customers.
- Tie SDK version to any release notes so we can surface breaks quickly.

References / links:
- Confluence pattern doc: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/DEVEXP/SDK+Telemetry+Patterns
- Starter repos: https://github.com/redwoodinc/sdk-starter
- Demo checklist (old): https://confluence.redwood.company/display/SE/Demo+Runbook
